open_engineering_issues: StairRunSpec defaults to 32 while the core erodes each tread separately and recipes explicitly use 36. The gladdm1 geometric certificate traverses 24-unit treads using neighboring support; this is a conservative planner/API contract issue, not proof of native invalidity. Audit union support and callers before changing the default.
The installed normal Windows Q2REPRO client requests foreground/focus at startup; render validation needs a non-hijacking engine path and engine-written screenshots.

Axial ramp navigation is deliberately bounded: one wholly clear continuous wedge, ordinary longitudinal end joins and conservative surrounding blockers. Arbitrary sloped surfaces, partial obstacle-aware ramp partitioning and native movement simulation are not implemented.

Palette selection must validate WAL flags/contents/value and compiled player-mask support. A typed solid graph and a resolved texture name alone did not reject Talus's initial water/warp mud1_1 material; retain this negative case when integrating material-role gates into default generation.

Default Q2 liquid material e1u1/water1 is absent from the current local stock asset tree, and generic liquid lowering writes surface flags/value0. Fold explicitly selects a verified WATER material with WARP|TRANS33 and no emissive flag; default-planner material-role validation remains outstanding.

Very short face-to-face passages can lose positive hull-center extent after erosion. Fold uses48-unit seams; overlap into rooms violates the current passage validator. This conservative construction contract is distinct from a native engine minimum corridor length.

Point lights inside liquid volume bounds are rejected by aggregate placement_in_solid validation (src/validator.cpp:609-617), despite valid native underwater lights. Lockyard uses dry/above-water lights; refine role-aware liquid placement without weakening solid collision gates.
The new compact generator retains the old target-player-count spawn policy: sampled duel maps have2 spawn positions and DM maps6. Spawn-pair occlusion does not establish adequate respawn diversity.

Lattice removes volume-CV and1280-center-distance preferences only for coherent marked2–8-room Q2DM/duel pools. Larger/unmarked/other-mode pools retain legacy weights. Remaining count inputs are adequacy heuristics; full-candidate physical ranking and human quality evidence remain open.

Bounded source-eye spawn refinement increases dense32-player regression cost; nearest24 supported alternatives and two passes cap the search. Normal and stress performance should be measured separately.
Remaining analytical lighting findings in generated rooms are retained; full VIS/light compilation does not establish client-rendered readability.

The historical Lattice example retained a larger envelope, more room hops and slicing gaps. Braid adds explicit wrapped_center construction for Q2 DM/duel with 5–8 rooms and separates its 16-case comparison from placement. Full native journeys, resource exposure and human flow remain open; unweighted room hops do not establish them.

The first Weft circuit protocol remains0/8. A separatelydeclared physical rescore is2/8 and16new earlier-turn trials pass; allfinishes arewall-adjacent and fivebroader stationdiagnostics fail. Open-space recovery and transfer toLattice remain untested.

Braid local spawn refinement is bounded to static common-floor AABB compact Q2 DM/duel layouts with 2–8 rooms, with exact valid-eye and per-pair occlusion checks. Spawn quantity and the 256-unit warning are unchanged; broader sizes, opponent pressure, native spawn selection and recovery remain untested.

Hinge demonstrates one optional upper connection at a time. Four-room controls stay outside scope and one scoped holdout selects no link. More links,192-height native journeys, route preference, open-space stopping and game-module resource/respawn behavior remain untested.
